activities.anchor: which geometry each element is playing
activities.caption: pair each load-carrying geometry with its trick
activities.name: ssGeoMatch

config.prompt: Five geometries, five material strengths — match them:

pairs.right: compression — thickness scales with height (Monadnock's 1.8 m base)
redirect load along a thrust line into pure compression
strength from geometry — a few centimetres of concrete roofing a stadium
steel's equal strength in tension — most material-efficient, least stiffness

config.why: Every real building is a combination; reading a section plan is recognising which geometry each element is playing.

config.q: Why do steel frames wrap around concrete cores in most tall buildings?
choices: Concrete's compression stiffness pairs with steel's tension strength — strength is a system property
Concrete is simply cheaper everywhere it is used
Fire codes require the core to be concrete for appearance reasons
config.why: The materials excel at different jobs — steel in tension, concrete in compression — and every tall building is a negotiation between them. The system is the load path, not the material certificate.

activities.anchor: would eat the floor area the building exists to rent
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the Eiffel Tower on twelve footprints
activities.name: ssColumnCloze

config.text: Twenty floors at 5 kPa on 1,000 m²: each floor presses 5,000 kN, so the base columns together collect %%0%% MN — the Eiffel Tower's weight. At an allowable 10 MPa, each of twelve columns needs %%1%% m² of section — nearly a metre square.
config.hint: One multiplication for the total, one division per column.

activities.anchor: sways out of phase with the building
activities.caption: rebuild the wind inversion — from constant gravity to the damper
activities.name: ssWindOrder

config.prompt: Put the tall-building escalation in order:
items: Gravity per floor is roughly constant — wind is not
The overturning moment grows with height squared
Sway grows with height to the fourth — codes limit drift to roughly h/500
Supertalls sprout stiffness: outriggers, tubes, diagrids, buttressed cores
Crosswind vortex shedding is countered by shaping and tuned mass dampers
config.why: Taipei 101's 660-tonne pendulum sways out of phase with the building — the lesson being that the real design limit is perceived motion, not stress.

activities.anchor: every element's position, not quantity, is the design
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the 15:1 tower's footprint
activities.name: ssSlimEstimate

config.prompt: 432 Park Avenue rises about 426 m at a 15:1 slenderness ratio. Roughly how wide is its plan?
config.why: 426 ÷ 15 ≈ 28 m — stiffness theatre in expensive dress.
config.context: Stiffness grows with the square of the distance material sits from the neutral axis — which is why the slenderest towers put everything in the perimeter.

activities.anchor: design for disassembly is now a scored criterion
activities.caption: file the frame options — against a real brief
activities.name: ssTimberBuckets

config.prompt: 'Advanced' is not a column in the table. File each choice against the brief that fits it:

items.label: a six-storey school on a tight carbon budget
a 60-storey tower on a hurricane coast
most long-span parking decks (a 1920s technology still winning)
panels that bolt together in days — programme as a structural property
embodied carbon around 300–500 kgCO₂e/m² of structure

config.why: Technologies are priced options against a brief — cheap or expensive, fast or slow, heavy or light in carbon, for a purpose.

statements.s: The dome's two problems are outward thrust at the base and compression at the crown — answered by buttresses and the oculus ring.
statements.why: The Pantheon has stood 2,000 years as the largest unreinforced concrete dome.

statements.s: Thin concrete shells carry enormous loads by curvature — material efficiency cantilevers cannot match.
statements.why: Nervi, Candela, Utzon's sails: form follows forces at its purest.

statements.s: Cable structures pay for axial efficiency with stiffness — their movement must be designed, not ignored.
statements.why: Suspension bridges and stadium roofs manage it with damping.

statements.s: Mass timber is the right choice for a 60-storey tower on a hurricane coast.
statements.why: The grid is deliberately indifferent to novelty — mass timber wins the school, loses the tower.
